newsitem.title: GERMANY: Krupp sees better oper profit in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Krupp sees better oper profit in 1997.

text.p: German steel and engineering group Krupp said on Wednesday it expected to post a better operating profit and pay a dividend again in 1997.
"The 1997 result will again ensure a dividend," said Gerhard Cromme, chairman of Fried. Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp, in remarks prepared for delivery at the company's annual news conference.

In 1996, the steel group posted 336 million marks ($197.5 million) in revenue from ordinary activities, down from 644 million marks the year before. Net profit was 208 million marks ($122.2 million), down from 505 million marks. It paid a dividend of five marks, unchanged.
Krupp, which recently merged its steel business with rival Thyssen AG after launching an unusual takeover bid, also expects business volume to expand this year, Cromme said.
"Krupp is confident it can make use of the improved economic situation and continued good export demand to broaden its business volume," Cromme said.
The negotiations with Thyssen are well under way, proceeding in a constructive manner, and plans are to make the merger retroactive to April 1, 1997, Cromme said.
"The future, joint, capable enterprise (Thyssen Krupp Stahl) will have the necessary size to reach internationally competitive costs and adequate market share," he said.
Orders and sales showed an uptrend in the first three months of the year, with orders rising 5.6 percent from the year earlier level to 6.5 billion marks.
-- Terence Gallagher, Bonn Newsroom, 49-228--26097150 ($ = 1.701 German Marks)
